findings.originalDescription: Anyone can self-register an email they don't own; when that person is later invited (staff or customer team), acceptance attaches the role to the attacker's account and discards the invitee's password
findings.originalStatus: FAIL — reproduced locally (attacker reached /staff/projects as developer)
findings.requiredFix: On accept: if the existing account is unverified, reset credentials, factors and sessions and quarantine its self-created org; otherwise require sign-in as that verified user. Refuse staff invites to existing customer accounts
findings.acceptanceTest: Register X unverified → invite X → accept with P2: P1 fails, P2 works, old sessions invalid; same for customer-team invite
findings.rootCause: acceptInvitation attached the invited role to any existing users row with the invited email, without proving the token holder owned that account; registration does not prove email ownership.
findings.evidence: 6 adversarial tests in tests/invitation-security.test.ts pass (staff takeover blocked, attacker MFA/sessions/tokens revoked, verified account requires sign-in, customer-team parity, staff→verified-customer refusal, concurrent single use); full suite 448/448; CI test check green on PR #26.
findings.notes: Awaiting Founder merge of PR #26 and the resulting Deploy staging run.

findings.originalDescription: Customer data export includes staff-only internal project and general-thread notes

Anonymous attacker can lock any account, including the Owner, indefinitely: the lock slides with each failure and the per-email limit returns 429 even to the correct password; no challenge on /login. Staging Owner email is public, and the lock also breaks staging deploy verification
findings.originalStatus: FAIL — code and local PoC; no branch fixes it
findings.requiredFix: Progressive throttling per account and IP, known-device bypass, count failures only, never extend a lock, Turnstile on /login after N failures, Owner unlock and alert
findings.acceptanceTest: 50 wrong passwords from 5 IPs → Owner on known device still reaches /mfa; lock never extends

findings.originalDescription: CRM contacts are linked at registration, before email verification, so an attacker's export contains a victim's CRM name and phone

findings.evidence: Test '[SEC-006] CRM contacts link only after the email is verified' passes: no link and no CRM data in the export before verification; linked (case-insensitive) after.
